## Avoid Sending SMS to Landlines with the Lookup v2 API and Go


SMS is one of the most effective ways of staying in touch with your customers. Why? Because:


- SMS delivery **isn't reliant on** **an internet connection**
- SMS are **delivered almost instantly**
- SMS works on **every mobile phone**
- SMS has an **open rate of 98%** ([according to Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2021/04/14/the-anatomy-of-sms-engagement/) )


But, what if you have an application where users have provided landlines as well as mobile/cell numbers? How do you filter out landlines so that you don't receive intermittent[errors](https://help.twilio.com/articles/360020693474-Error-30006-Message-Delivery-Landline-or-unreachable-carrier-when-Sending-SMS) and avoid paying for failed SMS.


Well, this tutorial will show you how to do so in Go using[Twilio's Lookup v2 API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api) .


## Prerequisites


To follow along with this tutorial, you'll need the following:


- A Twilio account (whether free or paid).[Create one now](https://twilio.com/try-twilio) if you don't have one already.
- A[Twilio phone number](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/phone-numbers) that can send SMS
- [Go](https://go.dev/) 1.23 or above
- A phone number that can receive SMS and a landline number (preferrably, one that belongs to you or a friend)
- Your preferred text editor or IDE for writing Go


## Build the Go application


The first thing to do is to create an empty Go project with module support. To do that, run the following commands wherever you store your go projects.


Copy code


```text
mkdir filter-landlines
cd filter-landlines
go mod init
```


### Add the required libraries


Next, the project will need a few dependencies, these are:


- [Twilio's Go Helper Library](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/introducing-twilio-go-helper-library) : This simplifies interacting with Twilio's APIs
- [GoDotEnv:](https://github.com/joho/godotenv) This loads environment variables from *.env* files


To install them, run the following command.


Copy code


```text
go get \
github.com/twilio/twilio-go \
github.com/joho/godotenv
```


### Set the required environment variables


You need to set two environment variables which are required to make authenticated requests to[Twilio's Lookup v2 API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api) . To do that, in the project's top-level directory, create a new file named *.env* and paste the configuration below into the new file.


Copy code


```text
TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=
TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN=
```


Then,[open the Twilio Console](https://1console.twilio.com/) in your browser of choice, and copy the **Account SID** , **Auth Token** from the **Workbench** at the bottom of the page.


Now, set the copied values as the values of` TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` and` TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` respectively, in *.env* .


Then, under **Quick actions** click **Phone numbers** , and copy an E.164-formatted phone number from the **Phone Number** column. Paste the phone number as the value of , and` TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER` in *.env* .


### Write the code


Now, it's time to write the code. Just one file. Create a new file named *main.go* in the project's top-level directory and in that file paste the code below. After that, replace` <A MOBILE PHONE NUMBER>` and` <A LAND LINE NUMBER>` with a mobile phone number and a land line, respectively.


Copy code


```text
package main


import (
"fmt"
"iter"
"log"
"os"
"github.com/joho/godotenv"
"github.com/twilio/twilio-go"
openapi "github.com/twilio/twilio-go/rest/api/v2010"
lookups "github.com/twilio/twilio-go/rest/lookups/v2"
)


func main() {
err := godotenv.Load()
if err != nil {
log.Fatal("Error loading .env file")
}


client := twilio.NewRestClient()
items := []string{"<A MOBILE PHONE NUMBER>", "<A LAND LINE NUMBER>"}
for number := range filterLandlines(items, client) {
err := sendSMS(client, number, os.Getenv("TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER"), "Here is your SMS")
if err != nil {
fmt.Printf("Unable to send SMS to %s! Reason %s.\n", number, err.Error())
} else {
fmt.Printf("SMS sent successfully to %s.\n", number)
}
}
}


func filterLandlines(phoneNumbers []string, client *twilio.RestClient) iter.Seq[string] {
return func(yield func(string) bool) {
params := &lookups.FetchPhoneNumberParams{}
params.SetFields("line_type_intelligence")
for _, number := range phoneNumbers {
resp, err := client.LookupsV2.FetchPhoneNumber(number, params)
if err != nil {
continue
}


if resp.LineTypeIntelligence.Type != "mobile" {
fmt.Printf("%s is not a mobile/cell phone number.\n", number)
continue
}


if !yield(number) {
return
}
}
}
}


func sendSMS(client *twilio.RestClient, recipient string, sender string, message string) error {
params := &openapi.CreateMessageParams{}
params.SetTo(recipient)
params.SetFrom(sender)
params.SetBody(message)
_, err := client.Api.CreateMessage(params)
if err != nil {
return err
}


return nil
}
```


The code above defines three functions:


- ` main()` : is the application's entrypoint. It starts by loading the environment variables registered in *.env* , before initialising a new Twilio` RestClient` object, and an array of phone numbers to validate using Twilio's Lookup v2 API. Following that, the code iterates over the list of phone numbers returned from calling` filterLandLines()` , and attempts to send an SMS to each one by calling` sendSMS()` . The user is notified whether the SMS is sent successfully or not through text printed to the terminal.
- ` filterLandLines()` : uses a custom iterator to filter landlines from an array of phone numbers, returning an iterator of strings. As the iterator iterates over the array, it attempts to fetch the details of each phone number from Twilo's Lookup v2 API including[Line Type Intelligence](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/line-type-intelligence) information. This information is necessary as it contains the phone number's type. If the phone number type is not set to "mobile", the number is not included in the returned iterator.
- ` sendSMS()` : is a small utility function that sends an SMS to the recipient with the message provided.


## Test that the code works as expected


With the code written, let's see it in action, by running the following command in a new terminal tab or session.


Copy code


```text
go run main.go
```


You should see output similar to the following printed to the terminal.


Copy code


```text
SMS sent successfully to +61123456789.
+15005550002 was identified as a landline.
```


## That's how to avoid sending SMS to landlines in Go with Twilio's Lookup v2 API


Thanks to the power of Twilio's Lookup v2 API and Go's standard library, you don't need to write much code at all to filter landlines from a list of phone numbers. Make sure you use this functionality to avoid being charged for failed SMS, and create more robust Go applications that integrate with Twilio.
